title: MCP Auth in Production: Issuer-Bound Enrollment and Tokens

questions.question: An MCP client discovers a different authorization-server issuer for the same resource. What should it do with its existing registration and access token?
options: Reuse only the access token after changing its audience locally
Enroll for the new issuer and keep credentials isolated by issuer
Reuse both because the MCP resource URL did not change
Store both under the tool name instead of the issuer
questions.explanation: Client identifiers and registration credentials belong to the authorization-server issuer that created them. An issuer change requires independent enrollment, and each access token is cached under both that issuer and its resource audience.

questions.question: Which enrollment approach is preferred by the MCP 2026-07-28 authorization profile?
options: RFC 7591 Dynamic Client Registration for every request
A Client ID Metadata Document served from the client's HTTPS URL
A protocol session that stores one global client identifier
A shared client secret embedded in every desktop client
questions.explanation: CIMD lets the authorization server resolve client metadata from an HTTPS client identifier. DCR is deprecated and remains only for compatibility.

questions.question: A deprecated DCR request describes a loopback desktop client. Which metadata is essential to classify it correctly?
options: Mcp-Session-Id
A wildcard redirect URI
application_type set to native
A reusable bearer token
questions.explanation: Current compatibility guidance requires the correct application type. A loopback desktop client is native; web clients use HTTPS redirect URIs.

questions.question: Why does the client validate the RFC 9207 iss value before redeeming an authorization code?
options: To prevent redeeming an honest issuer's code at the wrong token endpoint
To avoid refreshing the JWKS cache
To replace PKCE with issuer discovery
To select a tool from server/discover
questions.explanation: The issuer check defends against authorization-server mix-up. It complements PKCE by confirming the response came from the issuer recorded before redirect.

questions.question: Where should an MCP resource server cache authorization for the current stateless transport?
options: Under Mcp-Session-Id until the client sends DELETE
Inside the server/discover result for all later calls
In the SSE connection until it reconnects
Nowhere as a protocol-session decision; validate the bearer token on every request
questions.explanation: MCP 2026-07-28 removes protocol sessions. Each request crosses the authorization boundary independently, so identity, audience, expiry, and scope are checked each time.

questions.question: Which deployment evidence is strongest before trusting an authorization server?
options: The target server's discovered metadata checked against PKCE, issuer, enrollment, and resource-binding requirements
A vendor category table copied from an older lesson
A product page that says OAuth is supported
A successful login that does not inspect the token audience
questions.explanation: Capabilities change by deployment and version. The live discovery document is the concrete contract to check, followed by end-to-end issuer and audience validation.
